title: Paginate a list and take the last N items
problem: An API returns events a page at a time, and a dashboard shows the most recent events. Implement page(items, number, size) and last(items, n) in paging.py using slicing. Both must return new lists and must handle the edges: partial pages, pages past the end, empty input and n == 0.
requirements: page returns page `number` (1-based: page 1 is the first `size` items) as a new list
page returns [] for a page past the end, and the shorter remainder for the last partial page
page raises ValueError if number < 1 or size < 1
last returns the last n items as a new list, or all items if there are fewer than n
last returns [] when n == 0 and raises ValueError when n < 0
contract:
page(items: list, number: int, size: int) -> list
last(items: list, n: int) -> list
expectedBehavior: With 7 events and size 3: page 1 -> e1..e3, page 3 -> [e7], page 4 -> []. last(events, 2) -> [e6, e7]; last(events, 0) -> []; last(events, 10) -> all 7.
edgeCases: Last partial page and pages far past the end
number or size of 0 or below
last with n == 0 (the -0 trap) and n larger than the list
The result must be a new list: appending to it must not change the input
hints: Conceptual: a page is one slice, items[start:end]. Slices clamp out-of-range bounds and always return a new list, so pages past the end need no special case. Validation is the only `if` you need in page.
Specific: page `number` starts at index (number - 1) * size and ends size items later. For last, xs[-n:] breaks when n is 0 (-0 is 0); compute a non-negative start index from len(items) instead.

Implementation: in page, raise ValueError when number < 1 or size < 1, then slice from the start index to start + size. In last, raise for n < 0, then slice from len(items) - n, but make sure that start can't go negative (a negative start would count from the end).
evaluation: Each function is one slice plus validation: no loops, no manual bounds checks for 'past the end'
Correct for n == 0 and n > len(items) without special-casing every edge
